review.notes: All 16 democracy answers challenged; the equal-conditions answer corrected from Neutral to Disagree because opposition-party dissolution is implemented exclusion. Competitive elections, parliamentary confidence and courts overturning government remain counterevidence to unqualified personal dictatorship, while royal and military influence constrain accountability. Other 224 responses checked for completeness and axis independence, not independently researched anew; prior review preserved in revision 1. No score target. Existing flag and credits retained. Educated-assumption IDs recorded in the separate country review.

neutralAnswers.rationale: Educated assumption: Neutral / conditional is the most likely institutional interpretation of this specific proposition. Elections coexist with powerful unelected royal, military and judicial institutions, party dissolution and court removals of elected leaders. Government transitions during 2025 and Anutin’s December dissolution prevent treating a single cabinet as the entire year’s regime. Executive and unelected institutions constrain parliament, but ordinary lawmaking is not a general power to ignore an explicit legislative rejection. Emergency decrees within legislative constraints differ from overriding an explicit parliamentary rejection. The response reflects the identified competing institutional elements, rather than neutrality substituted for uncertainty. The sources do not document an official answer to this exact statement; the normative comparison and its stated trade-off remain uncertain.
